historical_record.description: Having recommended in January that the city buy the Allyne property at Green and Gough Streets for a park, the Recreation and Park Commission took the question up again at the Board of Supervisors' request. The National Society of Colonial Dames, owners of the lots next door, pledged $10,000 toward the purchase, and the Citizens Committee to Preserve the Allyne Property, with William W. Wurster as honorary chairman, wrote that the house was of both historic and architectural significance. The Commission agreed to allow six months after the city acquired the land for a group to propose restoring the house and keeping it as a public museum.

Told that the preservation committee had withdrawn its interest in the Allyne house, and that the Supervisors' parks committee wanted the property bought strictly as a park and not kept as a museum, the Recreation and Park Commission revoked its six-month offer and resolved that the property be acquired for park purposes only, asking for an official appraisal.

The Recreation and Park Commission asked for a $380,000 warrant to complete the condemnation of the Allyne property, Lots 2 and 3 of Block 544, from the estates of Lucy H. Allyne and Edith W. Allyne. At the California Heritage Council's request it had agreed two weeks earlier not to authorize demolition of the house for 90 days, while saying this did not change its plan for a park.

The California Heritage Council asked again to keep the Allyne house as a historical display. Burton Rockwell of the Art Commission said the local chapter of the American Institute of Architects endorsed saving it, and that the house had come around the Horn in pieces and been put together here. The city attorney advised that a museum would be a lawful recreational use, but the federal open-space grant of $114,000 had been approved on the understanding that the house would come down. The Recreation and Park Commission, two members dissenting, voted to go ahead with its original plan for a passive park.

Over a last appeal from the California Heritage Council, the Recreation and Park Commission approved a $3,372 service order to National Demolition Corp. to demolish the Allyne house at 2609 Gough Street, as the Board of Supervisors' purchase and the federal grant required.
